scopeNote: Buyer segmentation and publicly observable customer evidence for the eight mandated segments S1-S8; desk research only, no interviews, outreach, quotes, testimonials or willingness-to-pay.

sources.limitations: Third-party company-profile extract, largely marketing-derived; shows that multi-vessel yacht-management software is commercially offered, not that operators buy it in any volume.

claims.claimText: Owners modernising older boats describe uncertainty about which existing electronics will integrate with new equipment and are commonly advised to stay inside one manufacturer ecosystem.
claims.limitations: Three separate forum threads across three publishers; participants are self-selected owners and no sample or incidence is measured.

claims.claimText: Mixed-brand helms are described as constrained: radar and autopilot control can require same-brand equipment, and route-following behaviour differs between brands.
claims.limitations: Snippet-level extracts only; compatibility rules change by model and firmware and were not verified against manufacturer documentation.

claims.claimText: Some legacy analogue (resistive) sensors cannot be shared between two devices, which limits partial upgrades of older instrument systems.
claims.limitations: Single forum extract; technical claim not verified against manufacturer documentation.

claims.claimText: Receive-only AIS units are retailed by a UK chandlery in a band of roughly GBP 216 to GBP 637 excluding VAT across the listed Digital Yacht models.
claims.limitations: One retailer; page shows no price date; excludes antenna, splitter, cabling and installation. Offer existence is not sales evidence.

claims.claimText: An installer guide states that professional installation can add 15 to 50 percent of the hardware price, with complete multi-display helm rebuilds starting around USD 5,000 and exceeding USD 25,000 on complex yachts.
claims.observedValue: 15-50 percent of hardware cost; USD 5,000-25,000+ packages
claims.limitations: Installer marketing content, regional, illustrative; not an audited quotation survey and not a European price.

claims.claimText: NMEA offers installer training classes at USD 249 each and states that online training material alone does not award installer certification; certification requires scheduled virtual or in-person training and a 50-question exam.
claims.limitations: US association programme; other certification schemes exist; does not count certified installers or establish demand.

claims.claimText: NMEA positions NMEA 2000 certification as assurance that certified products interoperate, tested across electrical, visual/mechanical and interoperability areas.
claims.limitations: 2009 document reviewed as a search extract; certification is voluntary and does not guarantee every message or device combination.

claims.claimText: Signal K is an open-source local boat-data server and data standard that multiplexes NMEA 0183 and NMEA 2000 and supports community plugins and web apps.
claims.limitations: Project website; adoption, reliability in safety-critical use and commercial demand are not established.

claims.claimText: Navionics users publicly report steep price increases and coverage-boundary changes, and the developer reply attributes price and coverage changes to increased supplier cartography fees.
claims.geographicScope: Multiple countries, Czech App Store front
claims.limitations: Self-selected store reviews; the developer reply is a company statement, not an independent audit; storefront pricing varies by region.

claims.claimText: A marine vendor essay itemises common recurring nautical fees (for example charts at EUR 89/year, weather at EUR 79/year, AIS overlay at EUR 49/year, remote monitoring at EUR 39/year) and argues that several are not backed by continuing service.
claims.observedValue: EUR 29-179 per year per listed fee (illustrative)
claims.limitations: Vendor with a competing one-off-price product; figures are illustrative, not a price survey; citing them does not establish actual market prices.

claims.claimText: A certified autopilot system lost rudder-angle feedback, which disabled both autopilot and follow-up manual steering; the crew could not use the backup toggle-steering mode, and the investigation found training, labelling and drill gaps.
claims.limitations: Commercial roll-on/roll-off ship, not a recreational vessel; single occurrence; does not establish recreational failure rates.

claims.claimText: Spain registered 5,027 new recreational vessels in 2024, 15.9 percent fewer than 2023; rental registrations were 1,742 (-15.3 percent); 70.3 percent of units were 6 m or less and motor boats were 42.5 percent of the market.
claims.observedValue: 5,027 registrations; 1,742 rental; 70.3 percent <= 6 m; 42.5 percent motor boats
claims.limitations: Trade-press summary of ANEN/DGMM data; registrations are new-vessel transactions, not active fleet or aftermarket spend.

claims.claimText: Sailing schools are offered software covering multi-boat and multi-instructor scheduling, syllabus sign-off, certificate issue, instructor qualification expiry and per-boat maintenance logs.
claims.limitations: Vendor product page; it describes the operational need its product addresses but is not independent demand measurement.

claims.claimText: Marina operators are offered maintenance software covering planned and reactive jobs, compliance inspections, chargeable work, contractor coordination and reporting across multiple sites.
claims.limitations: Vendor page with marketing testimonials; not independent and not evidence of adoption volume.

claims.claimText: Boat owners discuss the value of remote monitoring and cheaper DIY alternatives (SIM router, cameras, bilge and high-water alarms), and some describe limited satisfaction with basic OEM monitoring.
claims.limitations: Two owner-community threads from the same Hanse/Cruisers Forum ecosystem; self-selected; no failure-rate or prevalence data.

claims.claimText: A public warranty complaint alleges a retailer required a commitment to buy replacement equipment before bench-testing a potentially faulty unit.
claims.limitations: Single complaint, no adjudication and no verified company response; illustrates a trust objection, not an industry practice.

claims.claimText: European Boating Industry states that the EU recreational boating sector comprises more than 6 million boats, more than 10,000 marinas and 48 million regular water-sports users.
claims.limitations: Industry-association advocacy figure reviewed as a search extract; aggregate with no segment or country breakdown.

claims.claimText: Owners debate touchscreen versus physical-control ergonomics for chartplotters, including wet or gloved hands and control during manoeuvres.
claims.limitations: Single thread; subjective opinions; no usability test or measured error rate.
